task.title: Behaviour-preserving refactor of kvparse.parser
task.statement: Refactor kvparse/parser.py without changing any behaviour. Two changes are requested. (1) parse_line(line) must be rewritten without the hand-rolled index loops: split the line at the first '=' with str.partition, strip the key and the value, raise ValueError when there is no '=' or the stripped key is empty, and remove one pair of matching surrounding quotes (both ends '"' or both ends "'") from a stripped value of length two or more; the function must not contain a 'while' loop. (2) Extract the detection of ignorable lines into a module-level function _is_ignorable(line) -> bool in kvparse/parser.py that returns True exactly when the stripped line is empty or starts with '#' or ';', and make parse use it. The observable behaviour of parse and parse_line must stay byte-for-byte identical for every str input: the same return values, the same exception types in the same situations (TypeError for non-string input to parse, ValueError for a malformed line), later duplicate keys still win, and quotes are removed only when the stripped value starts and ends with the same quote character (a value like '"x\'' keeps both characters; a lone '"' is kept). Exception messages are not prescribed. parse keeps raising TypeError for non-string input; what parse_line does with a non-string argument (for example a list or a mapping) is unspecified and must not be tested, because the required use of str.partition changes it. Keep the public names parse and parse_line exported from kvparse, do not modify the tests, and keep the existing suite passing.
acceptance_criteria: parse_line raises ValueError for '', 'novalue', ' = v', '   ', '=' and '\t= 1'.

parse behaviour unchanged: comments ('#' or ';' as the first non-blank character), blank lines and Windows line endings are handled as before; later duplicate keys win; parse('') == {}; parse('k = v') == {'k': 'v'}.
parse raises ValueError for a malformed line anywhere in the text and TypeError for non-string input (None, 3, a list, bytes).
kvparse.parser._is_ignorable exists, returns True for '   # c', '' and '\t; c', and False for 'a = 1' and 'a = # not a comment'.
The source of parse_line contains no 'while' loop and uses str.partition.
The existing tests in tests/ pass unchanged.

spec.restated_task: Refactor kvparse/parser.py while preserving its string-input behavior: replace parse_line's index loops with partitioning at the first '=', retain whitespace stripping and removal of exactly one matching outer quote pair, and extract blank/comment-line detection into a module-level _is_ignorable helper used by parse. interface_contract.name: kvparse.parser.parse_line (also exported as kvparse.parse_line)
interface_contract.behavior: For a string argument, use str.partition with '=' to separate the key from the value at the first occurrence. Strip both parts using default str.strip semantics. If the stripped value has length at least two and its first and last characters are both single quotes or both double quotes, remove exactly those two characters without further stripping or interpretation. Return a two-element tuple (key, value) of strings. Additional '=' characters belong to the value. Comment markers receive no special treatment in this function. The function must contain no while loop.
error_cases: ValueError: the portion preceding the first '=' is empty after stripping.
Non-string arguments: unspecified; no tests may impose behavior.

interface_contract.name: kvparse.parser.parse (also exported as kvparse.parse)
interface_contract.behavior: Retain the isinstance(text, str) input check. Iterate over text.splitlines() in order, use _is_ignorable to skip blank and whole-line comments, and parse each remaining original line with parse_line. Return a dict of string keys and values. Later occurrences overwrite earlier values for the same key; existing dictionary insertion order is preserved. Empty input returns {}. No inline-comment removal, escaping, interpolation, or value conversion occurs.
error_cases: TypeError: text is not an instance of str, including None, integers, lists, and bytes.
ValueError: any non-ignorable line lacks '=' or has an empty stripped key; the call raises rather than returning a partial result.

interface_contract.name: kvparse.parser._is_ignorable
interface_contract.behavior: Module-level helper returning a bool. For a string argument, return True exactly when line.strip() is empty or starts with '#' or ';'; return False otherwise. parse must use this helper for its skip decision. No package-level export is required.
error_cases: Non-string arguments: outside the specified contract.

acceptance_criteria: 1. parse_line uses str.partition with '=' to split at the first separator, contains no while loop, and replaces the hand-rolled index loops rather than reproducing them with another character-collection loop.

2. parse_line('a=b') == ('a', 'b'); parse_line(' a = b ') == ('a', 'b'); parse_line('a==b') == ('a', '=b'); parse_line('a = b = c') == ('a', 'b = c'); parse_line('a=') == ('a', ''); parse_line('k e y = v') == ('k e y', 'v').

3. Both matching single and double outer quotes are removed exactly once: parse_line('q = "x"') == ('q', 'x'); parse_line("q = 'x'") == ('q', 'x'); parse_line("q = ''") == ('q', ''); parse_line('q = ""') == ('q', '').
4. Mismatched quotes and lone quotes are retained: parse_line('q = "x\'') == ('q', '"x\''); parse_line('q = "') == ('q', '"'); parse_line("q = '") == ('q', "'").

5. Quote removal preserves all interior characters and whitespace: parse_line('q = " spaced "') == ('q', ' spaced ''); parse_line('u = "a" "b"') == ('u', 'a" "b'). Nested matching quote pairs are not recursively removed, and backslashes are not interpreted.
6. parse_line raises ValueError for each of '', 'novalue', ' = v', '   ', '=', and '\t= 1'. Exception-message text is unrestricted.

7. Default Python str.strip whitespace semantics are preserved for keys, values, and ignorable-line detection, including Unicode whitespace. parse_line itself does not split on line breaks or treat comment markers specially.

8. _is_ignorable exists at module scope, has a bool return annotation, and returns True for '', whitespace-only strings, '   # c', and '\t; c'; it returns False for 'a = 1', 'a = # not a comment', and 'a = ; not a comment'. Its predicate is exactly the specified stripped-line rule.
9. parse uses _is_ignorable to decide whether to skip each line and passes non-ignored original lines to parse_line.

limitations: Profile 'eval-attest-a1': inference provider codex_gateway; submission runs must use NVIDIA Nemotron on Nebius Token Factory and are labeled separately.

Sealed and adversarial suites run one child process per test under a supervisor that never imports candidate code and is the first step of its branch; two verifier canaries detect blanket result forgery. A candidate can still forge its own result from inside a child after the nonce was read if it spares the canaries (the mutation gate and held-out tests are the structural detectors).

The repository's own suite and the held-out suite run after the sealed verification in their own branches. They are bound through the same supervisor only for unittest repositories whose tests are statically discoverable; otherwise they are parsed from console output and the gate is labelled evidence_class 'stdout'.

Model-written sealed and adversarial tests can be wrong; their failures block VERIFIED. An independent arbiter classifies each failure (implementation bug, test defect or contract dispute) and, for pure test defects, offers a corrected module. The correction counts only after mechanical validation (same test methods, only the failing tests' bodies changed, passes on the candidate, still fails on the unmodified base or is caught by a mutant, with every result structurally sound and bound to its nonce); the corrected gate is then re-run and the verdict re-derived from the gates. A sealed test that failed by assertion or by an exception, whatever its origin, is never overridden (only a test the supervisor killed at its timeout may be corrected). The classification itself remains a model judgement.

A mutant counts as killed only when a sealed test failed with an authentic child result under a structurally sound supervisor run; lost, forged, incomplete, non-isolated, crashed or timed-out runs are unknown and excluded from the mutation score, and `attest check` recomputes the classification from the raw results.

INFEASIBLE is recorded only when a witness program written by the contract auditor demonstrated the contradiction by running on the unmodified repository (exit code and output recorded); the witness's logic is the model's, its execution is not.
Grounding runs only when the specification names external references; sources are cited, not verified for correctness.
